record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Multiple food sources in reinforced walks
record.original_question: How can the ant-inspired reinforcement model, in which random walks start from a nest and reinforce paths after reaching food, be extended so that several food sources are handled meaningfully, and what are the features of the limiting reinforced graph when this multi-food-source model is run on Z^2?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3 Extend the model so that it can take into consideration several sources of food in a meaningful manner. Identify the features of the limiting graph obtained on Z 2 .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following reinforced random walk model on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$. Fix a vertex $o \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, called the nest, and a finite set $F = \{f_1, \dots, f_k\} \subset \mathbb{Z}^2 \setminus \{o\}$ of vertices, called food sources. Successive "ants" (walkers) are released one at a time from $o$. Each ant performs a nearest-neighbor random walk whose step probabilities at any vertex $v$ are proportional to weights $w_n(e)$ assigned to the edges $e$ incident to $v$, where $n$ is the index of the current ant. In the single-source version of the model the ant walks until it first reaches the food, and then the weights of all edges traversed along its trajectory (or along a loop-erased version of it) are increased by a fixed amount, after which the next ant is released.

(a) Propose a precise extension of this dynamics to the case $|F| \ge 2$ of several food sources. The extension should be "meaningful" in the sense that:
 (i) each food source can act as an attractor that becomes reinforced by the ants that visit it;
 (ii) the process should not trivially reduce to single-source behavior in which only the food source closest to $o$ is ever used in the limit;
 (iii) the reinforcement rule should remain local and depend only on the past trajectories of the ants.

(b) For the dynamics proposed in (a), run on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with nest $o$ and food set $F$, describe the almost-sure structure of the limiting reinforced subgraph
$$G_\infty = \bigl\{ e \in E(\mathbb{Z}^2) : \lim_{n\to\infty} w_n(e) = \infty \bigr\}.$$
In particular determine whether $G_\infty$ is almost surely finite, whether it is connected, whether it contains a path from $o$ to each $f_i$, whether these paths share edges, and whether $G_\infty$ resembles a (Steiner-type) tree connecting $\{o\} \cup F$.
artifact.status_search_result: No mathematical result establishing a rigorous multi-food-source extension of ant-inspired reinforced random walks on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ together with an identification of the limiting reinforced graph appears in the literature. Related work treats either single-source ant-type reinforced walks (e.g., the directed edge reinforced random walk and its trapping in circuits on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\ge 2$) or biological/simulation-based foraging models with multiple food sources (e.g., Journal of Mathematical Biology 2024), but a rigorous probabilistic analysis of the multi-source limit graph on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ has not been carried out. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Directed Edge Reinforced Random Walk: The Ant Mill Phenomenon
status_evidence.snippet: On any finite graph which is not a tree, and on Z^d with d>=2, the Ant RW almost surely gets eventually trapped into some directed circuit which will be followed forever.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous results exist for single-source ant-type reinforced walks but not for multi-source extensions on Z^2.

status_evidence.title: Walk this way: modeling foraging ant dynamics in multiple food source environments
status_evidence.snippet: When multiple food sources are present but are not equidistant from the nest, at equilibrium all ants are in the trail connecting the nest to the nearest food source.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-food-source ant models have been studied at a modeling/simulation level, not as a rigorous probabilistic limit-graph result on Z^2.
